records.quote: Consider for illustration of the theorem 4.1, the sample X1, X2, X3, X4, X5 from U(0,1) with n = 4 and n + 1 = 5. Now we know that X_{k:n} ~ Beta(k, n + 1 − k). Now we take ℓ from Gumbel-Hougaard Copula ... as the appropriate stdf for Archimax copula model with 5-monotone Archimedean generator ϕ(t) = e^{−t^{1/θ}}, θ ∈ [1, ∞), where stable tail dependence function (stdf) is ℓ(x) = (x1^θ + x2^θ + ... + xn^θ)^{1/θ} with ℓ(x) = ||x|| A(x/||x||). For reverse hazard rate ordering, we calculate tϕ′(t)/ϕ(t) = −(1/θ) t^{1/θ} which is a decreasing function of t ≥ 0, because for θ ∈ [1, ∞), we get d/dt(−(1/θ) t^{1/θ}) = −(1/θ^2) t^{1/θ−1} ≤ 0 for all t ≥ 0. On the other hand F_{X5:5}/F_{X4:4} = x, F_{X4:4}/F_{X3:4} = x^4/(4x^3 − 3x^4) and equating both expression of ℓ we have A = n^{1/θ−1} with n = 4. Plots are shown below which illustrates the theorem 4.1 (i) for θ = 4.

conclusion.direction: X_{3:4} ≤rh X_{4:4} ≤rh X_{5:5}, verifying Theorem 4.1(i) graphically (Figure 1) at θ = 4

records.quote: To illustrate theorem 5.1, we will consider the random sample same as example 4.1 of section 4, Archimax sevival copula model with generator ϕ(t) = (1 + t)^{−θ} where θ ∈ [1, ∞), stable tail dependent function ℓ defined as ℓ(x) = (x1^θ + x2^θ + ... + xn^θ)^{1/θ}, where ℓ(x) = ||x|| A(x/||x||). (i) For hazard rate ordering, we calculate tϕ′(t)/ϕ(t) = θ/(1 + t) − θ which is a decreasing function of t ≥ 0, because for θ ∈ [1, ∞), we get d/dt(θ/(1 + t) − θ) = −θ/(1 + t)^2 ≤ 0 for all t ≥ 0. On the other hand (1 − F_{X1:4})/(1 − F_{X1:5}) = 1/(1 − x), (1 − F_{X2:4})/(1 − F_{X1:4}) = (1 + 8x^3 − 3x^4 − 6x^2)/(x − 1)^4 and equating both expression of ℓ we have A = n^{1/θ−1} with n = 4. Plots are shown below which illustrates the theorem 5.1 (i) for θ = 4.

records.quote: Suppose (X1, . . . , Xn) following PHR (B̄, α; ϕ1, A) and (Y1, . . . , Yn) following PHR (B̄, β; ϕ2, A) where ϕ1 and ϕ2 are Archimedean n-monotone generators for Archimax copula C_{ϕ1,A} and C_{ϕ2,A} respectively and B̄ the baseline servival function of the model. Then X_{n:n} (α; ϕ1, A) ≥st Y_{n:n} (β; ϕ2, A) if (i) β ⪯w α, ψ2 ∘ ϕ1 is super additive and (ii) ψ2 ∘ ϕ1 (t · A) ≥ A · ψ2 ∘ ϕ1 (t).

records.quote: Let X1, X2, ...., Xn be random variables, ϕ1 and ϕ2 are generators of n-dimentional Archimax copulas C1 and C2 respectively with inverse of ϕ2 is ψ2. If ψ2 ∘ ϕ1 satisfies the following, (1) Super-additive. (2) For A such that, 1/n ≤ A ≤ 1, ψ2 ∘ ϕ1 (t · A) ≥ A ψ2 ∘ ϕ1 (t), where A : [0,1]^n → [1/n, 1] is pickands dependence function as in equation (7). then C1 (x) ≤ C2 (x) for all x ∈ [0,1]^n.
